newsitem.title: USA: Assault charges dropped against singer Brown.
newsitem.headline: Assault charges dropped against singer Brown.

text.p: State prosecutors dropped charges on Thursday against singer Bobby Brown, who was due to stand trial for beating a Chicago man and nearly severing his ear in a bar fight in Disney World.

Charges against two co-defendants were also dropped after the victim, Neil Kelly, 38, reached an out-of-court settlement for an undisclosed amount, Brown's lawyer Robert Buonauro said. Kelly had demanded $6.6 million initially.

Brown and two companions were arrested in April 1995 while staying at a luxury Disney World resort. Police said the three men stomped and beat Kelly, 38, a Chicago medical technician, even after he lost consciousness. Kelly's partially severed ear was reattached at a hospital.

Police said Brown and Kelly began to argue after Kelly made advances to a woman socializing with Brown. The 27-year-old husband of pop diva Whitney Houston was facing a felony charge of aggravated battery and could have been sentenced to three years in prison if convicted.
Kelly informed prosecutors he would not come to Orlando for the trial.

"We can refile and we may well do that," prosecutor Bob Welch said in court. "That's a very, very strong possibility. We feel it's just appropriate to go ahead and resolve it through the court system."
Brown was not in court, which had been due to select a jury on Thursday.

"This thing has been about money from day one. Three or four people were minding their own business, then Mr. Kelly entered the scene," he said. Asked if Brown was relieved, his lawyer said: "At this point he is but he still has that cloud hanging over this."
